changes.how: In ownSpeedKind(), in the admin branch, replace the line 'if (segments.length === 4 && (segments[2] === "products" || segments[2] === "pages" || segments[2] === "articles")) return "product";' with two lines: a page's or an article's editor (segments.length === 4 and segments[2] is 'pages' or 'articles', and segments[3] is not 'new') returns 'category'; a product's editor (segments.length === 4 and segments[2] === 'products') returns 'product'. This holds for a store (/admin/{store}/pages/{id}) and for the platform (/admin/platform/pages/{id}), because segments[1] is not looked at. Update the function's comment: for the admin, 'category' is the page builder and 'product' a product's editor. No new kind is added: the admin never used 'category' (its label was 'Other pages'), and commerce.own_speed_samples has a check that allows only the five kinds, so reusing it needs no migration, in the same way the platform's rows already use 'product' for a theme's page.

commits.title: The morning briefing says when a kind of admin screen is not fast

changes.how: Add 'admin_slow' to AlertId. Add an optional field to PlatformSnapshot: 'adminSpeed?: SpeedRow[]' (import the type SpeedRow from './speed'). Export const ADMIN_SPEED_LOADS = 100. Export function adminSpeedAlerts(rows: readonly SpeedRow[]): PlatformAlert[]: for each row with row.loads >= ADMIN_SPEED_LOADS, look at its cells for the metrics 'lcp' and 'inp'; a cell whose rating is 'improve' or 'poor' (anything but 'good', and not null) gives one alert { id: 'admin_slow', severity: 'warning', values: { kind: row.kind, screen: row.screen, metric: cell.metric, value: cell.value }, href: '/admin/platform/capacity#speed' }. The 'good' lines are those of rateMetric() in src/lib/speed.ts (2.5 s and 200 ms): do not write the numbers a second time. In platformAlertsFor(), after the existing rules and before the sort, push ...adminSpeedAlerts(s.adminSpeed ?? []).

In platformSnapshot(), add ownSpeedReport('admin', now) from './own-speed' to the Promise.all and return adminSpeed: report.rows on the snapshot. In alertText(), before the final return, add: if (alert.id === 'admin_slow') return fillWords(w.admin_slow, { kind: adminText(lang, 'capacity').speed.kinds.admin[v.kind as SpeedKind], screen: adminText(lang, 'analytics').speed.screens[v.screen as SpeedScreen], metric: adminText(lang, 'analytics').speed.metrics[v.metric as SpeedMetric].short, value: speedValueText(v.metric as SpeedMetric, Number(v.value), locale) }) with speedValueText from '@/lib/speed' (`locale` is already defined at the top of alertText() as ADMIN_LANG_FACTS[lang].locale). sendPlatformBriefing() needs no change: it prints every alert.
In briefing.alerts (line 378 today) add: admin_slow: 'The admin is slow: {kind} on a {screen}, {metric} {value} at the 75th percentile over 28 days.'
The same key in briefing.alerts in Norwegian bokmål: 'Adminpanelet er tregt: {kind} på {screen}, {metric} {value} ved 75-persentilen over 28 dager.'

Add cases, building rows with speedRow() from './speed': (1) a 'category' computer row made from 120 samples with lcp 4,000 gives one admin_slow alert whose values name kind 'category' and metric 'lcp'; (2) a 'home' row from 120 samples with lcp 1,800 and inp 120 gives none; (3) a slow row from 99 samples gives none; (4) a row slow on inp only (inp 350) gives one alert with metric 'inp'; (5) a snapshot without adminSpeed gives no admin_slow alert; (6) the builder and the product editor are told apart: samples of kind 'category' and of kind 'product', one slow and one good, give exactly one alert, for the slow one.

Under '## The admin as people use it', after the October table and its paragraph, add: the briefing's rule (a kind of screen with 100 loads or more whose largest paint or interaction time at p75 over 28 days is not 'good' is a line in the platform's morning briefing), that the builder is its own row from this change (kind 'category' on site 'admin'), and two empty tables headed '28 days to <date>, after phase 0' and '28 days to <date>, after phase 2' with the columns kind, screen, loads, LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB, with the sentence 'Read from Platform, Usage and limits; a kind with 100 loads or more that misses 2.5 s or 200 ms gets a step in the plan.'
